target: Он учит русский, чтобы читать Толстого.
english: He studies Russian to read Tolstoy.
tip: чтобы (shtoby) plus an infinitive like читать (chitat = to read) means in order to, used when one subject does both actions.

target: Куда бы мы ни поехали, везде красиво.
tip: куда бы (kuda by) with ни (ni) means wherever, no matter where; the pair бы ни wraps the whole clause.

target: Она и красивая, и умная, и добрая.
english: She is beautiful, and smart, and kind.
tip: и (i) repeated before each item means both... and: и красивая, и умная, и добрая (i krasivaya, i umnaya, i dobraya).

target: Несмотря на то что шёл дождь, мы пошли гулять.
english: Despite the rain, we went for a walk.
tip: несмотря на то что (nesmatrya na to shto) is a fixed phrase for despite the fact that, used before a full clause with a verb like шёл (shyol = was falling).

target: Было так тихо, что слышно было, как тикают часы.
english: It was so quiet that you could hear the clock ticking.
tip: так (tak) plus что frames so... that: так тихо (tak tiha = so quiet), then что (shto) introduces the result.

target: В России две беды: дураки и дороги.
english: Russia has two troubles: fools and roads.
tip: две (dve = two) takes the genitive singular, so беда (beda) shifts to беды (bedy) after it, not the plural.
Dates use a neuter ordinal plus the month in the genitive: восьмое марта (vasmoye marta = the eighth of March).

english: A kind word is pleasant even to a cat.
tip: приятно (priyatna = pleasant) takes the dative for whoever feels it: кошке (koshke = to a cat), from кошка (koshka = cat).

english: Moscow wasn't built all at once.
tip: The reflexive ending -сь can make a verb passive: строилась (stroilas = was being built), Moscow is not building anything itself.

target: В гостях хорошо, а дома лучше.
english: It's nice to visit, but home is better.
tip: лучше (luchshe = better) is the irregular comparative of хорошо (harasho = good/well).

english: Ushanka is a fur hat with ear flaps.
tip: с plus the instrumental case means with something: с ушами (s ushami = with ear flaps).

english: Love is blind–you'll fall for anyone.
tip: Animate masculine nouns take a genitive-looking accusative object: козла (kazla = goat), not козёл (kazyol).

target: В России принято разуваться при входе в дом.
english: In Russia it is customary to take off shoes when entering a home.
tip: принято plus an infinitive states a custom with no subject: принято разуваться (prinyata razuvatsya = it's customary to take off shoes).
Russian counts toward the coming hour: половина пятого (palavina pyatava = half of the fifth) is 4:30, halfway to five. пятого is genitive.
